ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$ and $B$ are on the hyperbola $y=\frac{3}{x}$. Perpendiculars are drawn from points $A$ and $B$ to the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, respectively. If the area of the shaded region is $S_{\text{shaded}}=2$, what is the value of $S_{1}+S_{2}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $y= \frac{3}{x}$,\\
the area of the shaded region, $S_{\text{shaded}}=2$,\\
therefore $S_{1}+S_{\text{shaded}}=3=S_{2}+S_{\text{shaded}}$,\\
thus $S_{1}=1$, $S_{2}=1$,\\
hence $S_{1}+S_{2}=\boxed{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has coordinate axes and the hyperbola y=3/x in the first quadrant. Points A and B are both on the curve, with A in the upper left and B in the lower right. Perpendicular lines are drawn from A and B respectively to the coordinate axes, forming several rectangular regions: the area of the gray shaded rectangle in the lower left is S_shaded; the white region above the shaded region is labeled S1; the white region to the right of the shaded region is labeled S2. It can be seen from the figure that the shaded rectangle together with S1 is exactly the coordinate rectangle corresponding to point A, and the shaded rectangle together with S2 is exactly the coordinate rectangle corresponding to point B. Reasoning: If point (x,y) is on the hyperbola y=3/x, then the area of its corresponding coordinate rectangle is xy=x·(3/x)=3. Therefore, the area of the rectangle corresponding to point A is S1+S_shaded=3; the area of the rectangle corresponding to point B is S2+S_shaded=3. Given S_shaded=2, so S1=3-2=1, S2=3-2=1. Therefore S1+S2=1+1=2.
